_note: Core/LightSensor (F17.9) — the platform-neutral corpus for ambient light. A raw lux number is almost never what an app wants: it wants 'is this a dark room?' so it can dim a reader, or 'is this direct sun?' so it can raise the screen. Left to each caller that threshold is invented three times per app and differs across platforms, so the BUCKETS are pinned here with real illuminance references. The HYSTERESIS is pinned for a different reason: Android's TYPE_LIGHT fires on every hardware sample and the values jitter by several lux with no change in the room, so an unfiltered stream wakes the bridge dozens of times a second to say nothing. Read by kernel/test/lightsensor-conformance.test.ts (TS, reference), :core LightSensorConformanceTest (Kotlin) and Engine/iOS/LightSensor.swift.

category.name: a room with the lights off
the dark/dim boundary is exclusive on the low side
a thousand lux is daylight through a window
ten thousand is full daylight in shade
a nonsense negative reading is no light, not a separate category the hardware cannot distinguish

interval.name: absent falls back to a second
below the floor is hardware jitter, not light
above the ceiling clamps rather than refusing

emit.name: sensor jitter below the noise floor is silence
a change above the noise floor but under a tenth is still silence
a drop lands too — the rule is symmetric
a CATEGORY change always lands, even when the numbers barely moved
two lux is everything in a dark room
two lux is nothing in direct sun
from zero, anything above the noise floor lands
from zero, a sub-lux flicker does not
a non-finite reading is never delivered

sample.name: a negative hardware reading is clamped, because there is no negative light
a fractional reading is kept as read — rounding would lose a dark room's whole range
